versioning_note: v0.6.0 is the measured-comparison release. v0.6.1 is a presentation/documentation patch that promotes the measured three-model graph to the README front door, improves engineer/reviewer navigation, and adds a regression test protecting that structure. Runtime behavior and schema-v2 semantics are unchanged. Stable v1.0.0 remains deferred.
changes: Read-only WSL2 diagnostic CLI with environment diagnosis, RAW-bracketed probes, offline analysis, finite kernel-state observation, comparison, and Python environment checks.
RAW-origin acquisition scheduling with finite guard behavior and fail-closed schema-v2 completion verification.
Uncertainty-aware fixed-window rate analysis, adjacent signed REALTIME events, cumulative fixed-window REALTIME-minus-RAW evidence, and legacy v0.1 input support.
Read-only adjtimex(modes=0) observation with explicit Linux x86-64 LP64 ABI validation and structured unsupported/error states.
Method-aware comparison that preserves anomaly classifications and refuses numeric differences for incompatible or insufficient context.
Primary-source Microsoft/Canonical time-sync research with fresh-install versus upgrade caveats and no unsupported 24.04 backport claim.
Evidence-tiered README, D4R2 animated viewer, WSL host/kernel/guest architecture diagram, and dated upstream timeline.
Release-neutral documentation naming, preview security/support policy, and repository/package branding cleanup.
v0.4.0: publish the diagnostic core and reviewed presentation baseline to main while keeping the stable v1.0.0 contract deferred.

v0.5.0: docs/assets/clock-steering-story.svg (three architecture-state cards over a synchronized D4R2 replay) and docs/assets/three-model-timing-comparison.svg (three panels on one 0-120 s axis); README opening reordered with a 'How to read the figure' note; the step-by-step D4R2 replay moved next to the full table in docs/timesyncd-investigation.md.

v0.6.0: the three-model comparison's outer panels are now measured. Two read-only guest-side screens were taken on one Windows host on 2026-09-24 from fresh WSL boots with the project CLI: Ubuntu 24.04 with systemd-timesyncd active (about 4.8 % slow with +1.6 s REALTIME jumps every 34 s, tick 10000 -> 9437) and Ubuntu 26.04 fresh default (within +/-0.73 ppm, tick 10000). Raw probe/analysis/settle JSON, redacted environment snapshots, logs, hashes and the verbatim protocol are committed under evidence/2026-09-24-same-host-screens/ and described in docs/same-host-screens-2026-09-24.md.

v0.6.1: move the measured three-model comparison to the README front door; add concise engineering-depth and Windows/Ubuntu troubleshooting paths; refresh evidence-boundary copy; add a README front-door regression test. No runtime or schema behavior changes.

presentation_assets.three-model-timing-comparison.svg: README hero. Three panels share one 0-120 s axis and one symmetric-log +/-100,000 ppm scale with the +/-1000 ppm screen; cursors move together at ten times real time. Left panel (24.04, timesyncd enabled): the four 30 s enclosures from the 2026-09-24 same-host screen (-55,088.612 to -49,693.640 ppm, printed exactly in the chips and rounded outward in the headline; running means at 60/90/120 s are explicitly marked derived) drawn as deviation blocks, measured REALTIME jumps marked at 31, 65 and 99 s, the 300 s run in the final chip, tick 10000 -> 9437 in the panel summary, and the host clock offset in the caption. Middle panel (24.04 after the stop, D4R2, Windows QPC reference): t = 0 is the window opening about 60 s after the confirmed stop with the unit still enabled; the four published 30 s enclosures appear as each window closes, the 120 s enclosure appears at 120 s, PRE tick 10833 and POST tick 10000 are marked, and the 0-60 s and 0-90 s running means are labelled as derived. Right panel (26.04 fresh default, same host, same day): the four 30 s enclosures (-0.73 to -0.27 ppm) hug the zero line, the 300 s run appears at the final checkpoint. Checkpoint cards reveal immediately at 30/60/90/120 s, the first-window collection state is explicit, and the +/-100,000 ppm scale endpoints are labelled. Cursors and sampling washes are illustrative and hidden when animation is off; the static/reduced-motion state is the complete result. The footer records that W32Time was stopped and the host clock about 1.06 s behind NTP, that the result is guest-side only and not a ranking, and that the tick writer is not established. v0.6.1 promotes this asset to the first substantive element in the README after badges/tagline.
presentation_assets.clock-steering-story.svg: Shown in the 'What is actually unique here?' section. Card A (24.04 default) and card D (26.04 fresh default) show documented control paths; card A carries the C1 A0 REALTIME-step observation and card D the historical 300 s guest-side screen; card B (24.04 after systemctl stop) shows the measured D4R2 state with PRE tick 10833 and POST tick 10000 marked 'set by ?' / 'reset by ?'. The chart replays the four published 30 s MONOTONIC/QPC enclosures, the 120 s average and the RAW/QPC full-run enclosure; the only derived figure (about +0.80 s over window 1) is labelled derived; the static/reduced-motion state is the complete result.
presentation_assets.d4r2-settling-animated.svg: Step-by-step D4R2 replay embedded beside the full table in docs/timesyncd-investigation.md; published D4R2 interval enclosures only, coherent static/reduced-motion result.
presentation_assets.architecture-host-vm-guest.svg: Microsoft/Canonical default architecture is separated from project measurement points and bounded interpretation.
presentation_assets.upstream-timeline.svg: Vendor and project events are separate lanes; WSL 2.1.1 is identified as a prerelease and later Microsoft reports are not equated with #10006.

provenance: Fresh implementations of bounded acquisition/math ideas and public Linux interfaces. The committed 2026-09-24 evidence was produced by the repository's own read-only CLI on the reviewing machine; no historical private raw evidence or unrelated project data is copied into the repository.
